executiveSummary: Analysis of 21 surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent public health threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues to generate Elevated concern with ongoing animal-sector detections and human spillover risk in the Americas Region, representing a BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential. Mpox (BSL-3 select agent) remains active in the Americas with a dedicated April 2026 epidemiological update, while dengue, measles, and pertussis are driving sustained transmission burdens across the Western Hemisphere. The convergence of Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset, RSV co-circulation, and H5N1 persistence creates compounding respiratory threat conditions requiring coordinated surveillance response.
bottomLine: Multiple simultaneous epidemiological threats across the Americas and Europe—led by H5N1 avian influenza and mpox as BSL-3 select agents—demand heightened surveillance, cross-border coordination, and accelerated response capacity.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Dual PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained detection activity
BSL-3 select agent with documented zoonotic spillover to humans and pandemic potential
Animal sector detections continuing into Q1 2026 with human exposure risk at human-animal interface
Ongoing ECDC weekly threat monitoring through May 2026 suggesting persistent Euro-Americas threat landscape
threats.action: Activate enhanced One Health surveillance at human-animal interfaces; ensure H5N1-specific PPE and laboratory capacity; coordinate with FAO/OIE on poultry sector interventions; pre-position antiviral stockpiles and accelerate pandemic preparedness planning

threats.name: Mpox
signals: Dedicated PAHO epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 indicating active transmission requiring formal alert
BSL-3 select agent with sustained community transmission documented in multiple American countries
ECDC weekly reports through May 2026 indicating continued European monitoring of mpox signals
Ongoing clade surveillance needed to distinguish clade IIb from emergent clade I strains
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and ring vaccination with MVA-BN vaccine; enhance genomic surveillance to track clade evolution; ensure clinical recognition training for healthcare workers; coordinate cross-border case reporting

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating elevated case burden across the region
Historical precedent of record-breaking dengue seasons in 2024-2025 creating heightened baseline risk
Multiple serotype co-circulation increasing risk of severe dengue and antibody-dependent enhancement
ECDC weekly monitoring through May 2026 indicating importation risk to Europe via travel
threats.action: Intensify Aedes aegypti vector control programs; expand dengue rapid diagnostic capacity; prepare healthcare systems for surge in severe dengue cases; implement public communication campaigns on vector prevention

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses and Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO April 2026 alert marking official start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season with co-circulating respiratory viruses
Prior January 2026 PAHO alert specifically flagging simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation as a compounding threat
December 2025 alert documenting end of 2025 Southern Hemisphere season and start of 2025-26 Northern Hemisphere season indicating year-round pressure
Healthcare system capacity strain risk from dual-pathogen respiratory surge
threats.action: Accelerate Southern Hemisphere seasonal influenza vaccination campaigns; ensure RSV prophylaxis availability for high-risk populations; strengthen influenza-like illness sentinel surveillance networks; prepare ICU and pediatric surge capacity

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 3 February 2026 indicating active measles transmission requiring regional alert
Vaccination coverage gaps documented across multiple countries enabling outbreak conditions
Risk of re-establishment of endemic transmission in areas that previously achieved elimination status
ECDC weekly reports indicating measles as ongoing European concern throughout surveillance period
threats.action: Conduct urgent vaccination coverage assessments and targeted catch-up campaigns; strengthen measles-rubella surveillance and laboratory confirmation capacity; ensure outbreak response teams are pre-positioned; enforce vaccination requirements at borders and healthcare facilities

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 documenting sustained and worsening pertussis activity
Multi-country surge consistent with cyclical pertussis epidemic pattern following pandemic-era surveillance gaps
Infant mortality risk elevated in regions with low maternal Tdap vaccination coverage
Potential antimicrobial resistance emergence in Bordetella pertussis requiring macrolide resistance monitoring
threats.action: Strengthen maternal Tdap vaccination programs; ensure infant immunization schedules are maintained; enhance laboratory confirmation capacity; conduct AMR surveillance on Bordetella pertussis isolates

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 13 March 2026 indicating active yellow fever risk requiring formal alert
BSL-3 pathogen with high case fatality rate and vaccination-preventable transmission
Sylvatic transmission cycle activity suggesting epizootic spillover risk to unvaccinated human populations
Risk of urban transmission if Aedes aegypti vector populations are present in affected areas
threats.action: Verify yellow fever vaccination coverage in endemic and buffer zones; deploy emergency vaccination campaigns in outbreak-affected areas; strengthen epizootics monitoring in non-human primates; enforce international vaccination certificate requirements for travelers

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025 indicating hantavirus pulmonary syndrome activity requiring regional alert
High case fatality rate (30-50%) with no specific antiviral treatment available
Rodent reservoir population dynamics influenced by environmental conditions creating unpredictable spillover risk
Andes virus unique person-to-person transmission potential elevates containment complexity
threats.action: Enhance rodent control and public education on exposure prevention; ensure healthcare provider training on early HPS recognition; maintain isolation protocols for suspected Andes virus cases; strengthen syndromic surveillance in rural and peri-urban areas with rodent exposure risk

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents are actively flagged in current surveillance reports. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) (BSL-3) has generated dual PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026) documenting sustained animal-sector detections with ongoing human spillover risk across the Americas, representing the highest-priority pandemic threat in the current surveillance period. Mpox virus (Orthopoxvirus, BSL-3) is the subject of a dedicated April 2026 PAHO epidemiological update indicating active sustained transmission in the Americas Region, with ECDC concurrent monitoring suggesting European spread risk. Yellow fever virus, while not a CDC select agent, is a BSL-3 pathogen under PAHO alert as of March 2026. These detections collectively require BSL-3 laboratory surge capacity, specialized PPE protocols, and immediate notification to national biosafety authorities.
amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance monitoring warranted given sustained multi-country pertussis surge across the Americas with two PAHO alerts in four months
Influenza antiviral resistance (oseltamivir) surveillance critical given H5N1 activity and dual Northern/Southern Hemisphere influenza season pressure
Dengue treatment pathway integrity requires monitoring as no approved antivirals exist, creating pressure for off-label antimicrobial use in co-infected patients
General antimicrobial stewardship concerns elevated in context of multiple simultaneous outbreaks straining healthcare systems and potentially driving inappropriate antibiotic use for viral illnesses
emergingPatterns: Temporal compression of multiple concurrent epidemiological alerts across the Americas (February-May 2026) suggests cumulative healthcare system stress exceeding single-pathogen baseline capacity
H5N1 persistence across two consecutive PAHO update cycles (November 2025 to March 2026) without resolution indicates entrenched animal reservoir activity with unresolved human spillover risk

Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset (April 2026) overlapping with active dengue, measles, and pertussis surges creates differential diagnostic challenges and potential syndromic surveillance masking
Dual PAHO pertussis alerts within four months suggest a cyclical epidemic wave potentially amplified by pandemic-era vaccination coverage gaps that have not been fully recovered
Mpox maintaining sufficient transmission to warrant a formal April 2026 epidemiological update suggests incomplete containment of the post-2022 outbreak clade and possible endemic establishment

Methanol poisoning alert (October 2025) alongside GLP-1 medication misuse alert (February 2026) indicates expanding scope of PAHO surveillance to include chemical and pharmaceutical public health threats alongside infectious disease

ECDC weekly reporting cadence maintained continuously through 21 consecutive weeks (December 2025 - May 2026) indicates sustained elevated European threat assessment baseline with no return to routine monitoring intervals

Chikungunya formal alert (February 2026) combined with dengue and yellow fever alerts indicates Aedes-borne arboviral threat convergence requiring unified vector control response rather than disease-specific approaches
